environment: Organization: none — this is personal infrastructure, not an employer's. Primary use of Claude Code: homelab infrastructure-as-code (Ansible / k3s / Docker) development and operations

Source control: github.com/DanielH2018/server and its origin remote only. Repository visibility: PUBLIC — so only this repo's own work belongs in it, and content ported or first read from outside this session's repo is not its own work
Cloud provider(s): Cloudflare (DNS/proxy) and Backblaze B2 (Longhorn volume backup target), plus Cloudflare R2 for the rate-limit-sensitive backup tier. No employer cloud account is involved
Trusted internal domains: *.local.daniel-hunter.com (internal k8s/service hostnames) and the bare daniel-hunter.com, including auth.daniel-hunter.com and home-assistant.daniel-hunter.com

Key internal services: k3s cluster hosts daniel-box (control plane) and daniel-server (agent); daniel-pi (Docker, LAN-only). Traefik, Authelia/OIDC, Pi-hole DNS, Longhorn storage, CrowdSec, Uptime-Kuma, Prometheus/Grafana/Loki, Home Assistant — all internal, non-production personal infra

Org-specific CLIs: kubectl (authenticates as a read-only ServiceAccount by default), uv, prek, sops, k3s, chezmoi (dotfiles, separate repo), scripts/deploy.sh (takes a file lock), scripts/probe.py (read-only diagnostics)

Network posture: home LAN with WireGuard remote access (wg-easy on daniel-box, public 51820/udp; a second LAN-only instance on daniel-pi). Cloudflare-fronted public ingress via Traefik on daniel-box. daniel-pi is LAN-only and never internet-exposed

CI/CD deploy targets: GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/ci.yml) on PR and push to master, plus a pull-based GitOps deploy — a 30-minute systemd timer on daniel-box pulls origin/master and applies it with Ansible

Sensitive remote targets: pushing or merging to `master` in DanielH2018/server is a PRODUCTION DEPLOY — a systemd timer pulls origin/master every 30 minutes and applies it to the live homelab with Ansible. Also any namespace, host or container carrying `prod`/`production` as a whole word, and Longhorn PVCs plus their B2 backups, which are destructive-risk targets despite not being prod-named
Protected deployment namespaces / environments: the `homelab` and `longhorn-system` k8s namespaces

Protected IaC scopes: IAM/RBAC, networking, quota and node-pool resources; anything named or tagged prod/production; the k3s read-only ServiceAccount RBAC boundary (ansible/roles/setup/k3s); and CrowdSec/Traefik/Authelia auth-plane config

Secrets management: SOPS + age. ansible/vars/secrets.yml is age-encrypted CIPHERTEXT, committed to the public repo by design — editing or committing it in encrypted form is routine, not a leak. The sensitive artifacts are: the DECRYPTED plaintext of that file, anything under ansible/inventory/ carrying an inline secret value (that directory is not auto-encrypted), and the age private keys at ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt or any .agekey file, which must never be committed, printed or transmitted

Sensitive data locations & audiences: the age private keys and any decrypted secret plaintext — share with no audience. Internal package registry: none configured. Internal sharing / snippet hosting: none — treat public paste and gist services as outside the trust boundary. Trusted cloud buckets: none beyond the Longhorn backup targets named above
allow: Read-only kubectl against the homelab k3s cluster (get, logs, describe, top, events, explain, api-resources, diff) is routine and needs no confirmation — the default credential is a read-only ServiceAccount that cannot do anything else
Running the repo's own test and lint tooling is routine: `uv run pytest`, `prek run`, `ansible-lint`, and `uv run python scripts/probe.py` (read-only diagnostics)
Editing ansible/vars/secrets.yml through `sops` is routine — it is the sanctioned way to change a secret, and the file stays encrypted at rest

Git worktree lifecycle under .claude/worktrees/ is routine and fully reversible: creating, entering, removing a worktree, and deleting its merged branch (`git worktree add/remove`, `git branch -d/-D`, scripts/prune_worktrees.py). Several sessions work this repo in parallel and each owns its own worktree
Branch-level git that the reflog recovers — checkout, switch, rebase, merge, cherry-pick, stash push/apply — is routine local work in this repo
soft_deny: `kubectl drain` or `kubectl taint` against the k3s cluster (daniel-box / daniel-server), from any working directory — node-lifecycle disruption on a two-node cluster where one node holds the control plane. The built-in Node Lifecycle rule covers cordon/drain/uncordon but not taint. Clears only when the user names the node and the operation

Deleting or lifecycle-expiring objects in the Backblaze B2 or Cloudflare R2 Longhorn backup buckets, deleting Longhorn volumes, snapshots or backups through the Longhorn UI or API, or `helm uninstall` of longhorn — each destroys the same backup chain `kubectl delete` would, by a route no command pattern catches. Clears only when the user names the specific volume or backup and the operation

Running `scripts/deploy.sh` or `uv run ansible-playbook` WITHOUT `--check` against this inventory reconfigures live homelab infrastructure — Traefik, Authelia, Pi-hole DNS, WireGuard. Clears when the user asked to deploy, naming the service or the playbook
hard_deny: Never `git push` directly to `master` on DanielH2018/server. That branch is a production deploy trigger: a 30-minute systemd timer pulls origin/master and applies it to the live homelab with Ansible, so a direct push ships to running infrastructure without review. Changes reach master through a pull request whose CI has passed. Pushing to any other branch, and opening or merging a PR, are unaffected
